bib.title: Selection-Inference: Exploiting Large Language Models for Interpretable Logical Reasoning

read.skipped: Figures are images: per-task bar values in Fig 4b, 5, S1, S5 not readable.

question: Can splitting multi-step logical reasoning into alternating Selection and Inference LLM calls improve accuracy and give a causal, interpretable reasoning trace?
hypothesis: LLMs handle single-step inference well but fail at chaining steps; decomposing each step into selection and inference makes reasoning more accurate, generalisable and causal.
contributions: Evaluation of LLMs on 50 logical reasoning tasks showing good single-step but poor multi-step performance (Sec. 3)
The Selection-Inference framework, a modular iterative approach (Sec. 4)
7B model in SI almost triples vanilla and almost doubles COT on 10 tasks, often beating 280B baselines

method.summary: Frozen Gopher-family LLMs are prompted few-shot as a Selection module (picks facts by log-likelihood scoring over context sentences) and an Inference module (sees only the selection, generates a new fact appended to context). The loop runs a fixed number of steps; the last inference is the answer. A fine-tuned variant on ProofWriter is also tested.
method.task: multi-step logical reasoning over provided context (bAbI, ProofWriter)

datasets.name: bAbI tasks 1,2,3,15,16 (SI evaluation); 50-task suite from bAbI, BigBench, AAC, Jeopardy, ProofWriter, 2WikiMultiHop (Sec. 3)
datasets.preprocessing: bAbI SI answer = final word of last inference

datasets.name: ProofWriter OWA depth 0,1,2,3,5
datasets.preprocessing: Unknown-label examples removed; label True if any inference matches the statement, else False

inference.decoding: Selection: argmax summed token log-likelihood over context sentences (Alg 2); Inference: free generation, first sentence kept via regex r'[^.?!; \n]+'
inference.samples: single run per item; no seeds stated
inference.prompting: 5-shot; separate selection and inference prompts; vanilla and COT baselines also 5-shot

parameters.max facts per selection (ProofWriter): 2, with '. Therefore,' appended as a stop choice
parameters.steps: ProofWriter depth d run d steps (depth 0: 1 step); bAbI 1-3,15: 1 step; bAbI 16: 2 steps
parameters.halting: fixed number of steps; no halting function

other.fine-tuning variant (Sec 6): Inference LLM >99% test accuracy after 300 steps, batch 16; Selection LLM 4x10^4 steps, batch 16, 50 hours on a TPU; Selection predicts sentence labels; both trained on single steps; optimiser, lr not stated

metrics.name: Generative exact-match accuracy
metrics.definition: exact string match of first sentence, lower case, non-alphabetic characters ignored

metrics.name: Jaccard similarity of proof steps
metrics.definition: (M intersect GT)/(M union GT), exact string match over alphanumerics

eval.protocol: Two-sided proportions_ztest (statsmodels) on binary correctness; p values reported.

limits: Selection module is the main failure point and is hard to quantify without labelled intermediate steps (Sec. G).
No halting mechanism: fixed number of steps; results report only the final inference.
Context with all needed facts is assumed given; no retrieval.
Only deductive and a few inductive tasks; 10 of 50 tasks evaluated with SI.
Prompt engineering struggles with multi-step selection and number of rule arguments; lead shrinks with ProofWriter depth.
No seeds or repeated runs, temperature and lr not stated.
Gopher models are not publicly available; this is arXiv v1, numbers may differ from the ICLR 2023 version.
